sheet-1-1.description: The main part of sheet 1 covers the eastern residential blocks of Vincentown, a village in Southampton Township, at 50 ft to an inch. It is bounded on the west by Plum Street, drawn along the left edge of the sheet with only its east side built up, on the north by Chestnut Street, which runs east from Plum and then turns south-east, and on the south by Zelley's Alley, which crosses the foot of the sheet diagonally. Two streets run north-east from Zelley's Alley to Chestnut: an unnamed alley, lettered only 'Alley', and Pleasant Street. Lots fronting Plum Street (house numbers 225 to 248) carry frame dwellings, auto houses and stables, and the Town Hall with a jail at its rear stands on the east side of Plum. A cemetery fills the interior of the block between Plum Street and the alley. The block between the alley and Pleasant Street holds more dwellings and the Public School, a building marked as not used. North of Chestnut a row of lots runs up to vacant land, and east of Pleasant Street the land is lettered vacant beyond. A heavy line separates this part from the key map, the legend and the index in the upper right of the sheet and from the separately oriented railroad and factory district in the lower right, which is the second part of the sheet. Water pipes of 4 inches are drawn in Plum, Chestnut, Pleasant and Zelley's Alley, with fire hydrants at several corners. The sheet also carries the Sanborn title cartouche, population 1000, and notes on water facilities and the volunteer fire department.
notes: Chestnut is now Church Street; the unnamed Alley is now Browns Alley; Zelley's Alley is now part of Grange Street (OpenStreetMap names).
Town Hall with jail on Plum Street; Public School on Pleasant Street marked not used.
The key map (600 ft to an inch), legend, index and water and fire notes on this sheet are outside the mask.

Map, 50 ft to an inch. Title sheet with key map (600 ft to an inch, not georeferenced, outside both masks), index and water/fire notes. Part 1 (main map, left of the heavy line): Plum, Chestnut (now Church Street), the unnamed Alley (now Browns Alley), Pleasant and Zelley's Alley (now Grange Street); town hall, public school, cemetery. Part 2 (lower right, drawn at another rotation): Main Road (now Main Street north of Pemberton Road) at the road that is now Pemberton Road, with the Pennsylvania R.R. depot, Schank & Field hay press and Morris Canning Co.; placed from that single junction (anchored, low confidence). The north arrows on all sheets point about 19 to 20 degrees anticlockwise of the fitted north.

sheet-1-2.description: The second part of sheet 1, in the lower right of the sheet behind a heavy dividing line, shows the railroad and industrial district at the northern edge of Vincentown, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the page with its own north arrow. Its control is a single street junction: the road lettered Main, now Main Street north of the village, meets a road lettered only Road, now Pemberton Road, branching to the south-east. North-west of Main lie the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks of the Vincentown branch with a passenger station and a freight station on a wood platform, a stock yard and a storage building, and to the west a coal yard with hay, feed and office buildings. Beyond the tracks stand the works of Schank & Field, Inc., a hay and straw pressing and storage building with a thresher shed, a gasoline engine and a scale house with scales, and the large Morris Canning Co. canning factory, marked as not in operation, with a cement floor and a wood platform. A creek crosses the upper left corner. Much of the ground is lettered vacant beyond. Water pipes of 6 and 4 inches run along Main, with fire hydrants. The south-east side of Main is drawn only as an edge line, and the north-west side is open to the station grounds, so the street's width is not drawn. Because only one junction is available, the placement rests on that point, the assumed scale and the directions of the two roads.
notes: Main is now Main Street north of the village and the branch lettered Road is now Pemberton Road (OpenStreetMap).
The Pennsylvania Railroad line, depot and sidings drawn here are gone and are not in OpenStreetMap.
Morris Canning Co. canning factory marked not in operation; Schank & Field, Inc. hay and straw pressing and storage.
The part's north arrow points about 20 degrees anticlockwise of the north given by the two roads; the other sheets' arrows show the same offset.

Part 1 (main map, left of the heavy line): Plum, Chestnut (now Church Street), the unnamed Alley (now Browns Alley), Pleasant and Zelley's Alley (now Grange Street); town hall, public school, cemetery. Part 2 (lower right, drawn at another rotation): Main Road (now Main Street north of Pemberton Road) at the road that is now Pemberton Road, with the Pennsylvania R.R. depot, Schank & Field hay press and Morris Canning Co.; placed from that single junction (anchored, low confidence). The north arrows on all sheets point about 19 to 20 degrees anticlockwise of the fitted north.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the business centre of Vincentown at 50 ft to an inch, filling the whole sheet. Main Street runs down the right half from the Baptist Church at Chestnut Street to Zelleys Alley, with the post office, the Bank, general stores, a bakery, a drug store, a barber, a hardware and paints store, a blacksmith and wheelwright, the Washington House hotel and its stable, the M. E. Church, the Fire Dept. and the Sally Stretch Keen Memorial Library. Plum Street runs parallel to the east, lined with dwellings, and Chestnut Street joins the two at the top. Mill Street leaves Main westward and crosses the S. Branch of Rancocas Creek by an iron bridge, passing Trinity Church (Episcopal), an undertaker, a garage, a tin shop and a plumber, then crosses the mill race by a wooden bridge to the J. R. Wilkinson grist mill, drawn with its grain bins, smut machine and water power. The race and the creek, with a long backwater, fill the middle and left of the sheet, and the John B. Irick lumber yard with irregular and scattered piles of lumber occupies the ground between them. Race Street crosses the creek and the race near the foot of the sheet on its way to Main Street. A blacksmith hall and an ice house stand near the waterways. Water pipes of 6 and 4 inches are drawn in Main, Mill, Chestnut and Plum, with fire hydrants. The left half has no street junction of its own; its placement is carried from sheet 3, which draws the grist mill and the wooden bridge again.
notes: Chestnut is now Church Street; Zelleys Alley is now part of Grange Street (OpenStreetMap names).
Main Street at Mill Street carries a residual of about 5 m: the modern Mill Street curves into Main.
Iron bridge over the creek and wooden bridge over the race on Mill Street; J. R. Wilkinson grist mill run by water power.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, one part. Town centre: Main Street from Chestnut (Church Street) to Zelleys Alley (Grange Street), Mill Street west across the S. Branch of Rancocas Creek and the race to the J. R. Wilkinson grist mill, Race Street, Plum Street. West half has no street junction; held by five points carried from sheet 3 (grist mill and wooden bridge, drawn on both sheets).

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 shows the western end of Vincentown at 50 ft to an inch. Mill Street crosses the whole sheet from the fork at the left edge, where the Road to Mount Holly leads north-west and a Private Way leads south-west, east to the wooden bridge over the mill race and the J. R. Wilkinson grist mill at the right edge, which sheet 2 also draws. North of Mill Street are large deep lots with dwellings, auto houses, a store house, an ice house, a blacksmith and a second Private Way leading north; the land beyond is lettered vacant. Red Lion runs south from Mill Street to the foot of the sheet, with dwellings and a garage for 18 cars, and Race Street runs east from Red Lion toward the creek, crossed by an unnamed alley lettered Alley that links Race Street with the lots behind Mill Street. The mill race, lettered Race, runs down the right edge. Lot depths behind Mill Street are long and narrow, many with only a dwelling and an auto house. A heavy line cuts off the lower left corner, which holds an inset continuing Red Lion to the south, and the sheet's compass rose sits on that line. Water pipes of 6 and 4 inches are drawn in Mill Street, Red Lion and Race, with fire hydrants. Street widths of 50 and 40 feet are lettered on Mill Street and Red Lion.
notes: Road to Mount Holly is now Landing Street; the Private Way south-west of the fork is now Church Road; Red Lion is Red Lion Road (OpenStreetMap names).
The fork of Mill Street, Landing Street and Church Road is placed at the OpenStreetMap node; the parcel right-of-way centre there is about 12 m east of it.
Only three street junctions are on this part, so its fit has no redundancy.

Map, 50 ft to an inch. Part 1 (main map): Mill Street from the fork of the Road to Mount Holly (Landing Street) and a Private Way (now Church Road) east to the wooden bridge, Red Lion (Red Lion Road), Race, an unnamed alley, a second Private Way north of Mill. Part 2 (lower-left inset): Red Lion Road continued south (house numbers 15-24 and 45-51), drawn about 5 degrees off the main part; placed from a house drawn on both parts plus a point derived along modern Red Lion Road (low confidence).

sheet-3-2.description: The second part of sheet 3 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, behind a heavy line, continuing Red Lion south of the main part at 50 ft to an inch. It shows one street, Red Lion, about 40 feet wide, with house numbers 15 to 24 on the east side and 45 to 51 on the west side. The east side has a short row of lots with frame dwellings and auto houses; the head of the inset repeats a two-storey dwelling with a rear wing that is also drawn at the foot of the main part, and that house ties the two parts together. The west side is drawn only as a street line with house numbers and no buildings, and the ground beyond the lots on both sides is lettered vacant beyond. A 4 inch water pipe and a fire hydrant are drawn in the street. The inset is drawn about five degrees off the angle of the main part. There is no cross street in the inset, so its placement rests on the repeated house, carried from the main part, and on a point derived along the line of modern Red Lion Road at the sheet's scale. The upper part of the traced area, which repeats the main part, is left out of the mask.
notes: Red Lion is now Red Lion Road (OpenStreetMap).
Placed from three corners of a house drawn on both parts of the sheet and one point derived 530 ft south along modern Red Lion Road; low confidence along the street.
Smith Court, a modern street, would fall near the head of this inset; it is not drawn.

Part 2 (lower-left inset): Red Lion Road continued south (house numbers 15-24 and 45-51), drawn about 5 degrees off the main part; placed from a house drawn on both parts plus a point derived along modern Red Lion Road (low confidence).

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 covers the south-east of Vincentown at 50 ft to an inch and is turned on the page, with north about sixty degrees clockwise of straight up. Main runs across the top of the part from its junctions with Race and Zelley's, where it meets sheet 2, and then turns to run straight down the page to the foot of the sheet. Race comes in from the Mill Pond at the top. Zelley's runs south-east from Main to its junction with Plum St., and an unnamed alley lettered Alley continues from there south to Pleasant. Pleasant leaves Main east-north-eastward, passing dwellings and, at the right edge, the public school building. Along Main are close rows of stores and dwellings, a hardware store, a ware house and a coop, and the Grange Hall stands in the block between Main and Zelley's beside a cemetery. South of Pleasant, Main is lined by frame dwellings on deep lots with much vacant ground behind them. The Mill Pond, an arm of the creek, crosses the upper left, and the heavy line beside it separates the inset of Main Street farther south in the upper left corner. Water pipes of 6 and 4 inches are drawn in Main, Pleasant, Zelley's and the alley, with fire hydrants. Street widths are lettered on Main, Race, Zelley's and Pleasant.
notes: Zelley's and the Alley from Plum St. to Pleasant are both now Grange Street; Plum St. is Plum Street (OpenStreetMap names).
Grange Hall in the block between Main and Zelley's.
The sheet is drawn turned about 60 degrees on the page.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, turned on the page (north about 60 degrees clockwise of up). Part 1 (main map): Main Street from Race and Zelley's (Grange Street) south past Pleasant, Plum St., the alley now part of Grange Street, Grange Hall, cemetery, Mill Pond. Part 2 (upper-left inset): Main Street continued south (house numbers 301-311 and 343-353), Trinity Hospital; no junction, placed as the assumed continuation of part 1 (low confidence, along-street position uncertain by perhaps 5 to 10 m).

sheet-4-2.description: The second part of sheet 4 is an inset in the upper left corner, behind a heavy line, continuing Main south of the main part of the sheet at 50 ft to an inch and in the same orientation, so Main runs straight down the page. House numbers run from 301 to 311 on the west side and from 343 to 353 on the east side, carrying on from 313 and 354 at the foot of the main part. Both sides are lined with frame dwellings and auto houses on long lots, some with sheds, and an 80 ft distance to a frame shed is noted on one lot. Trinity Hospital, a small private hospital, stands at the lower left of the inset on the west side. The ground beyond the lots on the west is lettered exposure, and on the east the lots run back to the Mill Pond drawn in the main part. A 6 inch water pipe and a fire hydrant are drawn in Main, which is lettered 50 feet wide. There is no cross street in the inset, and modern Main Street is straight along this stretch, so the inset is placed as the direct continuation of the main part, matching a building cut at the foot of the main part with one cut at the head of the inset. Its position along Main Street is therefore uncertain by several metres, although its line across the street is held by the main part.
notes: Main is now Main Street (OpenStreetMap); Warrier Way, a modern street, would join it within this inset but is not drawn.
Trinity Hospital (private) on the west side of Main.
Placed as the assumed continuation of part 1 of this sheet; low confidence along the street.
